subject: Haldex Air Brake System Control Valves
summary: On February 6, 2009, Haldex Brake Products Corp. (Haldex) reported that certain air brake system control valves, distributed in 2008, contain a rubber diaphragm inside the quick release valve that may delaminate.Delamination of the diaphragm may cause significant levels of leakage and/or lead to the development of a bubble in the diaphragm that could trap air pressure in the valve.This condition can prevent a vehicle's service brakes from releasing properly. Malfunctioning service brakes can lead to risk of a vehicle crash.NHTSA assigned recall number 09E-004 to this matter. RMD mailed 24 Haldex customers, obtained through Haldex's amended Defect Report, an IR letter on April 6, 2009.RMD also requested an official list of all customers from Haldex on May 15, 2009.On June 5th, 2009, Haldex responded to RMD's IR letter with an additional 3 companies labeled as OEM Customers.Of the 27 initial IR mailings, all but 2 companies responded (Stewart & Stevenson and New England Mfg) for reasons unknown.8 of those companies chose to file a subsequent Defect Report for vehicles built with the recalled quick release valves.The remaining 17 companies were not required to issue safety recalls as they were distributors, not vehicle manufacturers, or had their parts remedied prior to installation.The corresponding EQ spreadsheet details each reason.One company, Meritor Wabco, filed a Defect Report for equipment (09E-023) re-branded under Meritor Wabco's trademark.This equipment was also further re-sold, so RMD mailed another 6 vehicle manufacturers on May 22, 2009.One manufacturer, Autocar LLC, already filed 09V-060 prior to the EQ.The remaining 5 companies all filed subsequent Defect Reports for their affected vehicles.A total of 13 subsequent safety recalls were influenced by this EQ.This EQ is closed.

subject: Bosch Hydraulic Disc Brakes
summary: On 4/1/09, Navistar notified NHTSA that it had decided certain Workhorse W22 series RV chassis, produced between July 24, 2000 and December 19, 2007, equipped with axles that include Bosch ZOPS or ZOHT pin slide hydraulic disc brakes were defective, and that the defect related to motor vehicle safety.Navistar stated vehicles whose use was occasional or seasonal, such as an RV, and which were equipped with these brakes may experience calipers sticking in the applied position.This can result in brake drag, abnormal heat generation, brake fluid boil, and extended stopping distances, increasing the risk of a crash.NHTSA assigned recall number 09V-110 to this recall.RMD mailed Bosch an IR letter on 4/23/09 requesting information about the defect, the affected customers, quantities shipped, and whether Bosch intended to file a Defect Report.On 5/7/09, Bosch responded stating that it did not agree with Navistar that a defect exists in the equipment, but a customer list was included and, with a confidentiality request, quantities sold to each company were included.Bosch listed 19 companies as receiving the subject hydraulic disc brakes.RMD mailed these 19 companies IR letters on 5/20/09.1 letter, to Athey Products, was undeliverable.17 companies responded with various statements, mostly claiming that their vehicle applications were not similar to recreational vehicles, or that they do not have warranty data pointing to a possible defect, or that the company is only a parts distributor not required to file a Defect Report.Navistar submitted a customer list of companies it sold its recalled chassis to under recall 09V-110.On 6/9/09, RMD mailed IR letters to 13 companies that received the recalled Navistar chassis equipped with Bosch brakes.5 companies chose not to file a Defect Report as the chassis manufacturer was already conducting a recall, but those companies did submit make/model information to RMD.4 companies submitted responses stating they did not receive those specific Navistar chassis.Another 4 companies (Damon Corp~09V-225, Gulf Stream Coach~09V-263, Triple E RV~09V-246, & Universal Specialty Vehicles~09V-263) chose to file Defect Reports for the vehicles they manufactured with the recalled chassis.Of Navistar's affected customers, another 5 companies (Fleetwood, Winnebago, Coachmen, Four Winds, & Airstream) had already filed their subsequent Defect Reports before this EQ was opened. Another company, National RV, is now out of business, so they were not contacted.Finally, on 6/30/09, RMD requested a list for ArvinMeritor's customers that were sold axles with the subject Bosch brakes.After many phone calls, letters, and e-mails, ArvinMeritor submitted a complete customer list on 4/19/10.RMD mailed IR letters to 4 companies identified as vehicle manufacturers on 4/26/10.North American Bus Industries sold all their units to Enjak, Inc.Enjak submitted a response stating they are only a dealer and not required to file a Defect Report.Both Spartan Chassis and El Dorado National submitted responses claiming that warranty history does not support the need for a safety recall of their applicable vehicles.Of the 37 companies contacted regarding these certain Bosch brakes, 4 chose to conduct subsequent safety recalls for their affected vehicles.A total of 10 companies overall (many before the opening of the EQ) chose to recall their affected vehicles.A spreadsheet of contacted companies and responses can be found in the document repository.This EQ is closed.

subject: CARRIER CORP. K410 CONDENSOR ASSEMBLIES
summary: ON APRIL 13, 2009, CARRIER REPORTED THAT CERTAIN K410 CONDENSER ASSEMBLIES, IMPORTED INTO THE UNITED STATES BEFORE DECEMBER 12, 2008, FOR USE ON SMALL BUS APPLICATIONS CONTAIN A COVER THAT MAY INTERFERE WITH THE ASSEMBLY'S COIL HEADER.INTERFERENCE BETWEEN THE COVER AND COIL HEADER MAY PREVENT THE FASTENERS FROM PROPERLY SECURING THE ASSEMBLY COVER.AN IMPROPERLY SECURED CONDENSER ASSEMBLY COVER MAY DETACH FROM A VEHICLE DURING OPERATION, POSSIBLY CAUSING A CRASH OR INJURY TO PEDESTRIANS.NHTSA ASSIGNED RECALL NUMBER 09E-013 TO THIS MATTER.RMD INITIALLY MAILED IR LETTERS TO 4 OF CARRIER'S CUSTOMERS THOUGHT TO BE VEHICLE MANUFACTURERS.TWO OF THOSE COMPANIES, DIAMOND COACH CORP. AND TRANSPORTATION COLLABORATIVE, FILED DEFECTS WITH THIS OFFICE (09V-201 & 09V-230).ANOTHER IR RECIPIENT, CT SOUTH, HAS REPLIED TO PREVIOUS EQ INQUIRIES STATING THAT THEY ARE A TRANSIT MANAGEMENT COMPANY AND NOT A MANUFACTURER OF MOTOR VEHICLES.PRO AIR INC. REPLIED THAT THEY DISTRIBUTED THE EQUIPMENT TO THREE CUSTOMERS.AFTER MAILING ADDITIONAL IR LETTERS, ELKHART COACH AND TIFFANY COACHWORKS FILED DEFECT REPORTS (09V-252 & 09V-278).THE THIRD CUSTOMER, GLAVAL BUS, HAD ALREADY FILED 09V-212 PRIOR TO THE OPENING OF THIS EQ.EQ RESPONSES CAN BE FOUND BELOW OR IN THE DOCUMENT REPOSITORY.THIS EQ IS CLOSED.

subject: TOW BAR ASSEMBLY FAILURE
summary: THE DEFECTIVE TOW BAR ASSEMBLIES INVOLVED IN THIS RECALL WERE SUPPLIED TO CHRYSLER FOR USE ON SOME OF ITS JEEP WRANGLER VEHICLES.THE PURPOSE OF THIS INVESTIGATION WAS TO IDENTIFY ANY ADDITIONAL PURCHASERS OF IDENTICAL OR SUBSTANTIALLY SIMILAR DEFECTIVE ASSEMBLIES AND TO INITIATE ADDITIONAL DEFECT REPORTING AND SAFETY RECALLS AS NECESSARY.TO ACCOMPLISH THIS RMD CONTACTED THE SUPPLIER OF THE ASSEMBLIES, VALLEY TOWING PRODUCTS, AND CONFIRMED NO OTHER SUCH ASSEMBLIES WERE DISTRIBUTED.THIS EQ IS THEREFORE CLOSED.

subject: FALLING BUS WINDOWS
summary: THE PURPOSE OF THIS INVESTIGATION WAS TO DETERMINE WHETHER THE TIP-IN STYLE TRANSOM WINDOWS SUPPLIED TO DAIMLER BUSES FOR USE ON BUSES IT MANUFACTURED, AND CONCERNING WHICH THAT COMPANY MADE A DEFECT DETERMINATION, WERE SUPPLIED TO ANY OTHER VEHICLE MANUFACTURERS OR AS REPLACEMENT EQUIPMENT AND, IF SO, TO PROMPT ADDITIONAL SAFETY RECALLS IF AND WHERE NEEDED.RMD ISSUED A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION TO THE WINDOWS' MANUFACTURER, HEHR INTERNATIONAL, INC. (HEHR) ON SEPTEMBER 2, 2009, INQUIRING ABOUT ITS DISTRIBUTION OF THE WINDOWS AND SOLICITING ITS OPINION AS TO WHETHER A SAFETY DEFECT EXISTED IN THOSE WINDOWS.HEHR RESPONDED ON OCTOBER 28, 2009, THAT IT HAD NOT SUPPLIED THE WINDOWS TO ANYONE OTHER THAN DAIMLER BUSES.IT ALSO OPINED THAT THE WINDOWS DID NOT CONTAIN A SAFETY DEFECT AND THAT ANY SCREW LOOSENING, AND CONSEQUENTIAL WINDOW COLLAPSE, WOULD BE DUE TO A FAILURE TO PROPERLY RETIGHTEN A SCREW AFTER MAINTENANCE, AS OPPOSED TO A DEFECT INHERENT TO THE DESIGN OR MANUFACTURE OF THE SCREWS OR WINDOWS.IN SUPPORT OF ITS OPINION, IT PROVIDED A SUMMARY OF HISTORICAL FIELD DATA AND ITS FIELD INSPECTION INVESTIGATION, NEITHER OF WHICH DEMONSTRATED ABERRANT PERFORMANCE.IT ALSO PROVIDED A SUMMARY OF TESTING CONDUCTED BY AN INDEPENDENT TESTING FACILITY DEMONSTRATING THAT THE SCREWS WOULD NOT LOOSEN AS MANUFACTURED. IN VIEW OF HEHR'S RESPONSE AND THE INFORMATION PROVIDED THEREIN, THIS INVESTIGATION IS CLOSED.

subject: VVA LINE WEAR AND OIL LEAKS
summary: THE PURPOSE OF THIS INVESTIGATION WAS TO REQUEST EACH VEHICLE MANUFACTURER IDENTIFY THOSE VEHICLE PRODUCTS ON WHICH IT USED THE DEFECTIVE CATERPILLAR C15 ENGINES AND TO REQUEST A DEFECT DETERMINATION BE MADE AS TO ITS VEHICLES, AS WELL AS SUBMISSION OF A DEFECT INFORMATION REPORT, OR AN EXPLANATION AS TO WHY ITS VEHICLES DO NOT CONTAIN A SAFETY DEFECT. RMD'S INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT BOTH OSHKOSH AND AMERICAN TRUCK USED THE ENGINES FOR MILITARY APPLICATIONS.ALSO, MONACO COACH CORPORTATION/CUSTOM CHASSIS PRODUCTS, LLC WAS PURCHASED IN BANKRUPTCY, AND SO NO DEFECT DETERMINATION COULD BE MADE ACCORDING TO ITS PURCHASER (NAVISTAR).AN INQUIRY TO COUNTRY COACH YIELDED A DEFECT DETERMINATION AND REPORT.THE REMAINING MANUFACTURERS (PETERBILT, KENWORTH, FREIGHTLINER, STERLING, WESTERN STAR, AND NAVISTAR) HAD FILED DEFECT INFORMATION REPORTS BY THE TIME OF RMD'S INQUIRY, SO NO FURTHER ACTION WAS REQUIRED AS TO THEM. IN SUMMARY, ALL APPLICABLE DEFECT DETERMINATIONS AND DEFECT INFORMATION REPORTS FOR AFFECTED VEHICLES HAVE BEEN RECEIVED AND THERE IS NO NEED TO CONTINUE THIS INVESTIGATION.

subject: Ricon 6-Way Power Seat Base
summary: On July 30, 2008, Ricon reported that certain 6-way power seat bases, produced between January 1, 2006 and May 14, 2007, contain a weld on the pivot shaft that may fail due to poor (cold) welding.A failed pivot shaft weld can cause the driver's seat to become detached from the seat base, possibly causing injury to the driver and increasing the risk of a crash.NHTSA assigned recall number 08E-046 to this matter.On February 5, 2010, the Recall Management Department (RMD) requested Ricon provide its customer list of all recipients that purchased the defective seat bases.Ricon did not respond.After several e-mail exchanges and a second IR letter mailed on April 2, 2010, Ricon responded with its customer list on April 9, 2010.RMD mailed IR letters to the 10 companies on Ricon's list.Those being: Siebert Mobility, Hoglund Bus Co., Inc., Ilderton Conversion Co, New England Wheels Inc, Northern Bus Sales, Inc., Sunset Vans, Inc., The Mobility Specialist, Thomas Bus Sales of IA, Vantage Mobility International, Malley Industries Inc.Only The Mobility Specialist filed a subsequent Defect Report with NHTSA for new vehicles it modified with these seat bases.It was assigned recall number 10V-270.RMD received responses from nine of the above companies.Eight of those companies were not required to file a Defect Report for their units for the following reasons:Hoglund Bus Co and Northern Bus Sales, Inc. sold their units over the counter and did not install the units.Siebert Mobility purchased only the assets from the former Arkansas Convention Center and Siebert was not provided any sales records for customer contact.Ilderton Conversion Co and Thomas Bus Sales of IA did not actually perform their installations but contracted them out to other companies.New England Wheels only installed their units on used vehicles.Malley Industries Inc. installed their unit on a Canadian vehicle.Vantage Mobility International (VMI) is a distributor that re-sold their units to 250 dealers.VMI did not file a Defect Report, as distributors are not required by regulation to do so, but did provide copies of the letters mailed to its dealer body.VMI's letters included verbiage about subsequent reporting responsibilities the dealers might have if they altered new vehicles and also included a template Defect Report for their convenience.Only three of VMI's dealers filed subsequent Defect Reports with NHTSA.They were: Arizona Mobility (10V-261), All in One Mobility (10V-271), Driving Specialties (10V-338).Only Sunset Vans, Inc. did not respond to RMD's April 20, 2010 IR letter.Another IR letter was sent to Sunset Vans on May 26, 2010.Phone calls and e-mail exchanges with Sunset Vans on September 1, 2010 did not motivate a response submission.A third IR letter was mailed on October 1, 2010.No response was received.Sunset Vans, Inc.'s lack of a response to RMD's recall inquiry will be forwarded to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel for further enforcement consideration and action.This EQ is closed.

welding.A failed pivot shaft weld can cause the driver's seat to become detached from the seat base, possibly causing injury to the driver and increasing the risk of a crash.NHTSA assigned recall number 08E-046 to this matter.On February 5, 2010, the Recall Management Department (RMD) requested Ricon provide its customer list of all recipients that purchased the defective seat bases.Ricon did not respond.After several e-mail exchanges and a second IR letter mailed on April 2, 2010, Ricon responded with its customer list on April 9, 2010.RMD mailed IR letters to the 10 companies on Ricon's list.Those being: Siebert Mobility, Hoglund Bus Co., Inc., Ilderton Conversion Co, New England Wheels Inc, Northern Bus Sales, Inc., Sunset Vans, Inc., The Mobility Specialist, Thomas Bus Sales of IA, Vantage Mobility International, Malley Industries Inc.Only The Mobility Specialist filed a subsequent Defect Report with NHTSA for new vehicles it modified with these seat bases.It was assigned recall number 10V-270.RMD received responses from nine of the above companies.Eight of those companies were not required to file a Defect Report for their units for the following reasons:Hoglund Bus Co and Northern Bus Sales, Inc. sold their units over the counter and did not install the units.Siebert Mobility purchased only the assets from the former Arkansas Convention Center and Siebert was not provided any sales records for customer contact.Ilderton Conversion Co and Thomas Bus Sales of IA did not actually perform their installations but contracted them out to other companies.New England Wheels only installed their units on used vehicles.Malley Industries Inc. installed their unit on a Canadian vehicle.Vantage Mobility International (VMI) is a distributor that re-sold their units to 250 dealers.VMI did not file a Defect Report, as distributors are not required by regulation to do so, but did provide copies of the letters mailed to its dealer body.VMI's letters included verbiage about subsequent reporting responsibilities the dealers might have if they altered new vehicles and also included a template Defect Report for their convenience.Only three of VMI's dealers filed subsequent Defect Reports with NHTSA.They were: Arizona Mobility (10V-261), All in One Mobility (10V-271), Driving Specialties (10V-338).Only Sunset Vans, Inc. did not respond to RMD's April 20, 2010 IR letter.Another IR letter was sent to Sunset Vans on May 26, 2010.Phone calls and e-mail exchanges with Sunset Vans on September 1, 2010 did not motivate a response submission.A third IR letter was mailed on October 1, 2010.No response was received.Sunset Vans, Inc.'s lack of a response to RMD's recall inquiry will be forwarded to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel for further enforcement consideration and action.This EQ is closed.

subject: CTS Corp Accelerator Pedal Assemblies
summary: On January 21, 2010, Toyota notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain model year 2007-2010 Toyota vehicles and certain MY 2009-2010 Pontiac vehicles contain a safety-related defect.Toyota stated that the accelerator pedal assemblies in those vehicles may become hard to depress, slow to return to idle when released, or may remain mechanically stuck in a partially depressed condition, increasing the risk of a vehicle crash.Further, Toyota stated that CTS Corporation (CTS) was the fabricating manufacturer of the defective accelerator pedal assemblies.NHTSA assigned recall number 10V-017 to this matter.RMD mailed an IR letter to CTS on February 1, 2010 with 23 questions regarding the recalled accelerator pedals.The IR questions requested information such as quantities manufactured, complete customer lists, part number changes, test results, chronologies, and extensive communications between CTS and Toyota.The letter also asked if CTS planned to notify its purchasers of a safety-related defect in its accelerator pedals.RMD requested that the first 7 questions, those involving customers and quantities, be answered by February 3, 2010 and the remaining questions within 30 days.After a granted extension request, CTS submitted its response to the first 7 questions on February 5, 2010.Confidentiality was granted by NHTSA's Chief Counsel's Office, but CTS detailed its customer list for all manufacturers it has sold accelerator pedals and listed all quantities sold.It was noted that subject pedals, those recalled by Toyota for containing a friction element of PPS or PA 4/6 material, were not sold to any other vehicle manufacturer. CTS officials chose to travel to U.S. DOT on February 17, 2010 to meet with ODI personnel.CTS explained the history of producing accelerator pedals for Toyota and expanded on the construction of the recalled pedals.CTS explained the recall issue with example pedals and test videos and asserted that unintended acceleration and a slower return to idle are not the same problem.CTS expressed that, in its opinion, unintended acceleration is not an issue with this pedal design, but, in rare cases in high humidity, there might be a slight delay in the return to idle position and that the pedal met the requirements of the applicable FMVSS even in that situation.After another extension request in early March 2010, CTS was allowed to produce the answers to the remaining IR questions on a time table ending on April 30, 2010.Extensive records were submitted including long e-mail strings between CTS, CTS Japan, and various global Toyota organizations.Detailed accelerator pedal diagrams, testing procedures and results, pictures, videos, field return records, and warranty rate information were all submitted as requested.NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel notified CTS on April 27, 2010 to submit everything that it had prepared already, but not to gather any further information unless requested by the agency.Virtually all of CTS' submissions were granted confidentiality as they contained sensitive business and commercial information.However, the core question of an Equipment Query investigation, whether the same or similar equipment was sold to any other vehicle manufacturer for inclusion in a new motor vehicle, was given in CTS' original submission on February 5, 2010.CTS did sell accelerator pedal assemblies to other vehicle manufacturers, but they were pedals of a different design consisting of different materials than those at issue in Toyota recall 10V-017 (and GM recall 10V-018 for the Pontiac Vibe).(Continued on attachment)

subject: IMMI Seat Custion Locking Mechanisms
summary: On February 1, 2010, Indiana Mills & Manufacturing, Inc. (IMMI) notified NHTSA that it sold certain school bus seats, manufactured between October 6, 2009 and January 25, 2010, and that these seats did not meet FMVSS No. 222, School bus passenger seating and crash protection, when installed in a school bus application. IMMI stated that certain seat cushion locking mechanisms are capable of being misaligned during vehicle assembly or after the vehicle is in use. A seat cushion with a misaligned locking mechanism might not be able to meet the requirements of FMVSS No. 222 as it would not allow the cushion to remain attached to the seat during a certain threshold of upward force. Should a school bus seat cushion become detached from the seat during vehicle operation, personal injury is possible to the seat occupant(s).On April 2nd, 2010, RMD mailed IR letters requesting 573 Defect Report submissions to 13 of the 14 purchasers IMMI listed in its February 1st letter to the agency.Daimler Trucks (Thomas Bus) had already filed a Defect Report for its buses in February (10V-058).After a second IR letter was mailed to the other 13 purchasers on June 17, 2010, RMD received a response from all purchasers with the exception of Durham School Services.As a school bus operator and not a vehicle manufacturer, they would not be required to notify the NHTSA and submit a Defect Report, but RMD did want to notify them of this safety issue.Of the 12 respondents, 4 chose to file a subsequent Defect Report for school buses they built with these seats:Collins Bus Corp:10V-291 Starcraft Bus: 10V-194 Bus West: 10V-292 HA Dehart & Sons: 10V-142The remaining 8 responses did not require a Defect Report as the vehicles were repaired prior to sale, the seats were previously returned to IMMI, or they were not installed into buses as original equipment.This EQ is closed.EQ responses can be found in the Document Repository.A working spreadsheet of responses can be found by clicking on the paper clip in this Adobe document.

subject: Remy Alternator Fires
summary: On April 2, 2010, Remy Power Products, LLC (Remy) reported that certain alternators, produced between December 19, 2009, and February 22, 2010, contain an internal voltage regulator that can become damaged by transient voltage that may occur when the regulator and the alternator are built, tested, and installed. Should the regulator's circuit be damaged, thermal degradation of the circuit can occur, increasing the risk of a fire or heat damage even when the vehicle is off. NHTSA assigned recall number 10E-010 to this matter.On April 14, 2010, the Recall Management Division (RMD) requested Remy provide its customer list of all recipients that purchased the defective alternators.Remy responded with an e-mail that contained insufficient contact information for those recipient, and accordingly mailed Remy and information request (IR) letter for the complete information on April 28, 2010.That same day, RMD mailedDaimler Trucks and Knopf Automotive, who were listed as recipients and for which RMD had additional contact information.Daimler Trucks responded that all defective alternators they received had been returned to Remy.RMD never received a response from Knopf Automotive.Previous EQ mailings have revealed that Knopf is a distributor that would not have an obligation to notify NHTSA of a safety defect or contact a recall campaign.RMD received a more detailed customer list from Remy on June 3, 2010, listing 90 purchasers and over 20,000 alternators.RMD then issued IR letters to those companies that re-sold the equipment under another brand/trademark, mostly automotive retail chains.On July 21, 2010, RMD mailed IR letters to Associate Jobbers Warehouse, AutoZone Parts, PASCO, General Parts, O'Reilly Automotive, and Bosch Canada.Only General Parts chose to recall the alternators (10E-036) they sold under their trademark, Proven Value.The others, Associate Jobbers Warehouse, AutoZone, and O'Reilly, responded that they supplied Remy with customer lists of purchasers.Bosch Canada sold their inventory only in Canada.PASCO responded that they do not actually re-label their purchased alternators.Our regulatory authority does not extend to products sold abroad or to distributors.Additionally, We do not believe our regulations are sufficiently decisive as to whether re-branders of equipment (other than tires) must take responsibility for a defective product they sell under that brand name, to include conducting a recall campaign.Accordingly, we decline at this time to pursue further those re-branders.This EQ is closed.IR responses can be found in the EQ repository. A working spreadsheet of response summaries can be found on the next page.

subject: Daimler Engine Unexpected Shut Down
summary: The Office of Defects Investigation (ODI), Recall Management Division (RMD) conducted a review of safety recall 10E-005.In a letter dated March 16, 2010 Daimler Trucks North America LLC (Daimler) reported that certain Detroit Diesel EPA07 Series 60 engines, produced between January 1, 2007 and April 20, 2009, with software versions earlier than V62.6 ZGS 114 were defective, and that the defect related to motor vehicle safety.These engines, installed as original equipment in emergency vehicles, contain software which may cause the engine to shutdown unexpectedly when a Diesel Particulate Filter over temperature condition is detected.Unexpected emergency vehicle engine shutdown could hamper rescue operations and put first responders and or the public at risk.NHTSA assigned recall number 10E-005 to this matter.This EQ was opened to track the disposition of affected engines sold to the other manufacturers noted in Daimler's Defect Report.RMD mailed information request (IR) letters to four of the six manufacturers listed in Daimler's Defect Report.Spartan Chassis (10V-181) and Pierce Manufacturing (10V-195) had both filed subsequent Defect Reports for their affected vehicles prior to this IR mailing.Three of the four companies RMD mailed also filed a Defect Report for their affected vehicles.They are:Sutphen Corporation - 10V-416 Kovatch Mobile Equipment Co. - 10V-386 American LaFrance - 10V-227Only Progressive Industries, Inc. did not file a Defect Report.In a letter submitted to RMD dated August 25, 2010, Progressive noted that its eight affected engines were re-sold to Pierce Manufacturing, who had already submitted their report to NTHSA in May.Sufficient action has been taken by all the manufacturers RMD contacted and all affected vehicles identified.This EQ is closed.

subject: Dimplex Fireplace Remote Control Kits
summary: On May 11, 2010, Skyline Corporation notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain model year 2004-2007 Skyline Park Model trailers contain a safety related defect.Skyline stated that certain trailers were originally equipped with Dimplex electric fireplaces containing a plug-in remote control receiver that can overheat, possibly causing a fire.NHTSA assigned recall number 10V-201 to this matter.In early May 2010, Thor Industries contacted the Recall Management Division (RMD) regarding the use of these Dimplex fireplaces in several of its recreational vehicles.Upon initial contact with Dimplex, it was learned that these fireplaces were sold through a distributor that may sell them to many other recreational vehicle manufacturers to be installed as original equipment.Dimplexissued a recall with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (#10-167) for 700,000 units.In May 2010 RMD informed Dimplex of its responsibilities under 49 CFR 573 as to its obligations to conduct a safety recall for the original equipment used in motor vehicles by more than one vehicle manufacturer.Dimplex submitted its Part 573 Report (10E-027) on June 6, 2010, identifying a total 25,000 defective units sold to its distributor, WESCO International, Inc. (WESCO).On July 6, 2010, RMD mailed WESCO an Information Request (IR) letter requesting a full list of customers that were sold these recalled fireplaces.WESCO responded on July 23, 2010, with a listing of 162 companies that were further sold this equipment.After parsing out closed companies from the list and those known to RMD not to further distribute motor vehicle equipment or manufacture vehicles, RMD contacted a total of 40 companies with IR letters mailed on August 31, 2010.On November 1, 2010, RMD mailed a second round of IR letters to 14 companies that had not yet responded to the first letter.By the end of December 2010, another 2 IR letters were mailed to Wray Brothers and Rexhall Industries, as they had still not responded to RMD's letters.As of the closing of this EQ, despite multiple phone calls, e-mail exchanges, and IR letters, these two companies have still not filed an official response with RMD regarding this matter.RMD will refer this matter to the Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for further enforcement activity as appropriate.Of the remaining 38 companies RMD contacted, their responses break down as follows:- 23 vehicle manufacturers filed a Part 573 Report with NHTSA and contacted their affected customers.- 6 letters were returned as those companies are no longer operating.- 4 companies only used the units for samples/prototypes and did not retail them to the public.- 3 companies either did not receive any affected units or only sold their units outside the U.S.market.- 1 company, R-Vision, responded that their company filed bankruptcy and they no longer possessedcustomer records for those vehicles affected by the Dimplex equipment.- 1 company, Custom Campers, is owned by NuWa Industries and their affected units were included in NuWa's Part 573 report to NHTSA. For detailed responses, please see the attached spreadsheet outlining each company's response to NHTSA's IR letters.This EQ is closed.

subject: Webasto Sunroof Separation
summary: On August 10, 2010, Webasto notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain Hollandia 600/700 & Hollandia TVS 900 aftermarket sunroofs contained a safety related defect. Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

Webasto stated that these sunroof models, manufactured between 2002 and 2010, may experience an adhesive bond failure where the sunroof glass attaches to its frame. This failure increases the risk of the glass detaching from the vehicle and causing injury to other motorists or pedestrians.This recall was assigned number 10E-038. Webasto and its counsel met with RMD on August 18, 2010 to discuss the recall's next steps. RMD learned that the majority of these products are installed by a third party, on new motor vehicles that have not yet been retailed, often at the request of a new car dealership. These installers are required to notify the NHTSA of any new vehicles they altered by way of a Part 573 Defect Report. On September 2, 2010, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Webasto requesting a list of companies who purchased the defective sunroof models.Webasto replied on September 9, 2010, submitting a purchaser list to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) for confidentiality consideration.NCC granted this confidentiality request as the release of Webasto's purchaser list could cause substantial competitive harm.Due to the large number of companies that purchased these sunroofs, RMD worked with Webasto to ensure notifications to Webasto's authorized installers (AIs) included instructions on how to file a Defect Report with NHTSA should one be required.For those AIs that altered new vehicles (vehicles not yet delivered to the first retail purchaser), the AI notification letter offered guidance on how to submit a Defect Report to NHTSA and instructions that a third party, Impartial Services Group, LLC (ISG), would be contacting them to obtain VIN information for vehicles they altered as new.ISG obtained VIN information from each AI and returned to them a computerized list of vehicle year, make, and model as this information is necessary for a Defect Report submitted to NHTSA.ISG then utilized the acquired VIN information to notify the current registered owners about the safety recall. On July 5, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 87 AIs that had previously communicated to Webasto that they had maintained vehicle VIN records for their past alterations, but had not yet sent those records to ISG.Forty-five (45) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter, however, some did take action by submitting their records to ISG.RMD chose to mail a second IR letter on April 19, 2012, to 8 AIs who were identified as having the largest quantities of sunroof installations that needed to be recalled.Four (4) companies responded by filing Defect Reports with NHTSA and sending their affected VINs to ISG for consumer notification.The information for the 4 nonresponsive companies: Automotive Concepts, Classic Auto Interiors & Accessories, Dundalk Glass Center, and Kenny?s Auto Stylist will be forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action at their discretion. With an ISG generated vehicle list and a Defect Report, RMD received safety recalls from 111 AIs recalling over 74,000 vehicles.It is very likely that more AIs contacted ISG and Webasto to submit their records of affected vehicles, but failed to notify the NHTSA of their actions.Webasto has mailed over 231,000 owner notification letters to vehicle owners that have recalled sunroof assemblies.This investigation is concluded as we believe we have realized the safety benefits that can be reasonably achieved through an Equipment Query of this scope.This EQ is cl

subject: Caterpillar Engine Fuel Line Leak
summary: On June 22, 2010, Caterpillar, Inc. reported that certain C7 diesel engines, manufactured between March 3, 2005 and January 6, 2009, contain two fuel lines that may develop a crack at the fastening point to the common fuel rail and cause a fuel leak.A fuel leak, in the presence of an ignition source, can result in a vehicle fire.This issue was assigned recall number 10E-025.On October 30, 2010 the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed two Information Request (IR) letters to both General Motors (GM) and Kenworth Truck Company (Kenworth) as they were the only two manufacturers that had not yet filed subsequent safety recalls for their vehicles.PACCAR, Kenworth's parent company, submitted a response on November 2, 2010 stating their recalled C7 engines were only used in prototype chassis that were not retailed to the public.GM submitted their response to RMD on November 5, 2010 claiming they did not agree that an unreasonable risk to motor vehicle safety was present in their vehicles as a result of these recalled Caterpillar engines.These C7 engines were installed into 356 Chevrolet and GMC C-Series Medium Duty Trucks.GM stated that their underhood thermal safety team reviewed the situation on July 1, 2010 and concluded that a leak from the suspect pipe does not constitute a safety risk since no hot surfaces or ignition source is located near the potential leak.GM stated that it only had one warranty claim for repair of a C7 engine fuel line with no comments as to the root cause and no reference to any safety concern.GM also included a Powerpoint presentation from the company's safety analysis, which is included in the EQ repository.However, GM did provide its VIN list of affected vehicles to Caterpillar so Caterpillar could proceed with their recall remedy.GM's response will be forwarded to the Medium & Heavy Duty Vehicles Division for any further analysisThis EQ is closed.

subject: Trans/Air TA73 Evaporator Melting
summary: On June 22, 2010, Trans/Air Manufacturing (Trans/Air) reported that it had decided certain TA73 evaporators, manufactured between August 2, 1999, and May 15, 2007, contain a safety related defect.Trans/Air reported that these evaporators contain a power resistor to regulate blower speed.Should a short occur in the low or medium speed circuit while the blower is in high speed, the short may cause the resistor to melt and possibly ignite the plastic blower housing to which it is mounted.A melted blower housing could result in a fire.This issue was assigned recall number 10E-028.On December 8, 2010, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed Information Request (IR) letters to 7 vehicle manufacturers on Trans/Air's customer list.All 7 manufacturers responded to RMD's IR letter.Glaval Bus had filed their subsequent Defect Report before receiving RMD's IR letter and it was given recall number 10V-618.It was discovered that Coachmen RV's bus assets were purchased by a company called All American Group.After research with Trans/Air, All American Group discovered that no past Coachmen units were affected and they were accidentally included on Trans/Air's customer list.Trolley Enterprises responded that they had gone out of business in July 2010.Previous employees are presently searching for any remaining customer records and will forward them to RMD if recovered.The following Defect Reports were received as a result of this EQ:10V-637 - Micro Bird School Buses 10V-645 - Micro Bird Transit Buses 10V-641 - Elkhart Coach 10V-652 - Coach & Equipment Manufacturing Corp. 11V-091 - Double K. Inc.This EQ is closed.

summary: On June 22, 2010, Trans/Air Manufacturing (Trans/Air) reported that it had decided certain TA73 evaporators, manufactured between August 2, 1999, and May 15, 2007, contain a safety related defect.Trans/Air reported that these evaporators contain a power resistor to regulate blower speed.Should a short occur in the low or medium speed circuit while the blower is in high speed, the short may cause the resistor to melt and possibly ignite the plastic blower housing to which it is mounted.A melted blower housing could result in a fire.This issue was assigned recall number 10E-028.On December 8, 2010, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed Information Request (IR) letters to 7 vehicle manufacturers on Trans/Air's customer list.All 7 manufacturers responded to RMD's IR letter.Glaval Bus had filed their subsequent Defect Report before receiving RMD's IR letter and it was given recall number 10V-618.It was discovered that Coachmen RV's bus assets were purchased by a company called All American Group.After research with Trans/Air, All American Group discovered that no past Coachmen units were affected and they were accidentally included on Trans/Air's customer list.Trolley Enterprises responded that they had gone out of business in July 2010.Previous employees are presently searching for any remaining customer records and will forward them to RMD if recovered.The following Defect Reports were received as a result of this EQ:10V-637 - Micro Bird School Buses 10V-645 - Micro Bird Transit Buses 10V-641 - Elkhart Coach 10V-652 - Coach & Equipment Manufacturing Corp. 11V-091 - Double K. Inc.This EQ is closed.

subject: Norcold Refrigerator Fires
summary: On October 7, 2010 Norcold, Inc. (Norcold) notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain 1200 series refrigerators, manufactured between January 1, 2003, and October 6, 2010, contain a safety related defect.Norcold stated that certain refrigerators contain either a sensing algorithm or a thermal switch to interrupt power to the refrigerator when it detects high temperatures that could lead to a fire.Norcold intends to install a thermocouple to improve the response time of this high temperature detection and further reduce the possibility of fire within these units.Should a fire occur within a refrigerator installed into a recreational vehicle, both personal injury and property damage are possible.This issue was assigned recall number 10E-049.On December 14, 2010, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed an information request (IR) letter to Norcold requesting a list of customers who purchased the same or similar defective refrigerators.Norcold responded to RMD's IR letter on December 21, 2010, with a list of companies that were further sold this equipment.On January 3, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 55 companies from Norcold's customer list known to manufacture vehicles or alter new vehicles.On August 8, 2011, RMD mailed another IR to 6 companies that did not respond to the first request for information.In total, 39 companies filed responses with RMD.Of those companies that responded, 23 filed Defect Reports with NHTSA and conducted safety recalls for their affected vehicles.12 companies responded that they did not install the defective refrigerators into new motor vehicles.One company, Gulfstream Coach Inc., filed their Part 573 Report prior to the opening of this EQ.Three companies, Country Coach Corp., Trail Lite, and H&H Trailer Company, responded that their companies were previously liquidated and their new companies did have the needed records to conduct safety recalls. INC.(11V-052) SUPERIOR COACH INTERIORS, INC.(11V-449) T&E ENTERPRISES(11V-075) TECHWORKS INC.(11V-484) TRAIL BOSS CONVERSIONS, INC.(11V-083) TRAVEL UNITS INC.(11V-056) TRIPLE E RECREATIONAL VEHICLES(11V-138) UNITED SPECIALTIES INC.(11V-087)A summary of IR responses can be found attached with this closing resume.This EQ is closed.

subject: Siemens Circuit Breakers Failing
summary: On November 11, 2010, Siemens Corporation (Siemens) notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain plug-in circuit breakers, manufactured between June 1, 2010, and July 31, 2010, contain a safety related defect.Siemens stated that certain circuit breakers contain a spring clip that may break or fail due to improper heat treatment during manufacturing.Should a circuit breaker spring clip break or fail, excessive temperature, arcing or thermal damage leading to a fire is possible.Should a fire occur from a circuit breaker installed into a recreational vehicle, both personal injury and property damage are possible.Siemens noted that these circuit breakers were sold under both the Siemens and Murray brand names and installed into load centers and meter combo enclosures manufactured between June 23, 2010, and August 25, 2010.This issue was assigned recall number 10E-053. Coachmen RV originally reported this issue in a Part 573 Report for their vehicles on September 15, 2010.When this EQ was opened in December 2010, only Coachmen RV, Dutchmen RV, and Keystone RV had filed subsequent Part 573 Reports for vehicles they manufactured with these circuit breakers.In response to an information request (IR) letter Siemens stated that all of their circuit breakers sold for possible use in motor vehicles were purchased by Dave Carter & Associates, a motor vehicle equipment distributor.Dave Carter & Associates' IR response noted that it sold the affected circuit breakers to Coachmen, Forest River, Keystone RV, Fleetwood RV, and Dutchmen RV.Keystone RV and Dutchmen RV had previously filed Part 573 Reports for their units, recalls 10V-606 and 10V-589, respectively.Coachmen had also filed their Part 573 Report, recall 10V-433, prior to the opening of this EQ.On July 26, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to Forest River and Fleetwood RV.Forest River responded on August 9, 2011, that after researching the circuit breakers they purchased, their Coachmen division was the only group that used the equipment in their vehicles.Coachmen filed their Part 573 Report in September 2010, recall 10V-433.Fleetwood RV responded to their IR letter by filing a Part 573 Report on August 1, 2011, recall 11V-399, to remedy their affected motor homes.As all vehicle manufacturers using these defective circuit breakers in their vehicles have responded with appropriate measures to recall their products, this Equipment Query is closed.

subject: IEE Passenger Sensing System Mats
summary: On December 17, 2010, General Motors (GM) notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain 2005 - 2007 model year Cadillac CTS vehicles contain a safety related defect.GM stated that certain CTS vehicles contain a passenger sensing system mat, manufactured by IEE, in the front passenger seat that may flex causing the mat to kink, bend or fold.If this flexing causes the connections in the mat to break, the passenger airbag could become disabled.Non-deployment of the front passenger air bag in the event of a crash necessitating that air bag's deployment may reduce protection of the passenger and increase the risk or severity of injury to them.This issue was assigned recall number 10V-644.On February 8, 2011, RMD mailed an information request (IR) letter to IEE requesting a list of purchasers for any company that was sold the same or similar defective mats.RMD also requested IEE supply the year, make and models of compatible vehicles for each of the mats it listed in its response.IEE responded on February 15, 2011, reporting that the mats recalled in GM recall 10V-644 were developed specifically for the 2005-2007 Cadillac CTS.IEE noted that, ...the CTS Sensor Mat is not the same or similar to any other sensor mat manufactured by IEE.IEE further explained that the sensor mats were sold to Lear Corp. (Lear), for incorporation into seat assemblies, with the seat assemblies finally being sold to GM.Also, some sensor mats were sold to Integrated Manufacturing and Assembly, LLC (IMA) who would then re-sell the mats to GM to use as service parts.Ultimately, these parts were all sold to GM for use in the 2005-2007 Cadillac CTS vehicles.According to its 10V-644 Defect Report, GM reported that some vehicles outside the recall population have ...significantly lower incident rates and will be provided a special coverage.This special coverage includes a free repair should the same issue occur to non-recalled 2005-2007 Cadillac CTS vehicles up to 10 years or 120,000 miles.On April 7, 2011, RMD mailed an IR letter to GM to gather more information on GM's decision to only recall a portion of the vehicles that contained the subject IEE mats.RMD also requested that GM provide updated to current warranty claims, field reports, and other field information for CTS vehicles both recalled and those under the special coverage.On May 19, 2011, GM responded with a letter and several CD attachments that were submitted to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel along with a request for confidentiality.GM confirmed that the IEE mats recalled in 10V-644 were only used in the 2005-2007 Cadillac CTS.GM also explained its reasoning in only recalling a portion of the CTS vehicles containing IEE mats.Due to various production phases, error detections, and false corrections, certain vehicles were more prone to mat failures than other vehicles.GM identified 4 distinct seat assembly production periods and chose to recall CTS vehicles depending on which seat assembly each vehicle received.Examining the data submitted in regards to warranty claims, field reports, and incidents, the CTS vehicles that were included in the safety recall were responsible for about 80% of the overall claims.CTS vehicles included in the special coverage (essentially an extended warranty), those with seat assemblies from other identified production phases, were responsible for about 20% of the overall claims.As GM has provided clear data to support its recall decision and since no other manufacturer has installed these same or similar passenger sensing system mats / seat assemblies in their vehicles, this Equipment Query is satisfied.This EQ is cl

subject: Carrier A/C Evaporator Fires
summary: On January 25, 2011, Carrier Corporation (Carrier) notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain GenV EM-1 evaporator assemblies, installed into school buses and shuttle buses, contain a safety related defect.Carrier stated that certain EM-1 evaporators, manufactured between January 2006 and December 2010, contain a Delphi Pack-Con III fuse holder in an Allied Motion motor assembly.Over time, the Delphi fuse holder contacts may relax and possibly produce arcing.If sufficient arcing occurs, the fuse holder may melt, and may be accompanied by flame, smoke and potential fire.This issue was assigned recall number 11E-003.On February 2, 2011, RMD contacted Delphi Corporation (Delphi) via e-mail to learn if it intended to file a Part 573 Report for the Pack-Con III fuse holders that Carrier deemed defective in its Part 573 filing.On February 17, 2011, Delphi responded via e-mail that this particular fuse holder had been in production since 1976 without any field issues reported to Delphi.Delphi stated that it, ...believes the Pack-Con III fuse holder is not defective and that the Pack-Con III fuse holder was misapplied by Carrier.On March 17, 2011, RMD issued an information request (IR) letter to Delphi to formally request a list of purchasers that received these fuse holders.On March 25, 2011 Delphi responded by supplying a list of purchasers to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel under a request for confidentiality.Given the information supplied in Delphi's earlier February 17, 2011 response, RMD chose not to contact the purchasers of these fuse holders during this EQ as no other vehicle or equipment manufacturers have filed similar safety defect decisions with the NHTSA at this time.RMD may, however, contact these fuse holder purchasers in the future should any other safety defect decisions regarding this equipment be filed with the NHTSA.On October 6, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 10 purchasers identified in Carrier?s Part 573 filing in order to learn if any vehicles were manufactured with these EM-1 evaporators.Six manufacturers responded by filing Part 573 Reports for vehicles they manufactured and also conducted safety recalls.Three manufacturers, Sonny Merryman Inc., Colonial Equipment Company, and Rivers Bus Sales responded that their evaporators were only installed into used vehicles or retail sold, neither requiring the companies to conduct safety recalls.Pro Air, LLC (Pro Air) responded that it distributed its more than 5,400 units to companies that might manufacture new motor vehicles.After multiple requests, RMD received Pro Air?s purchaser list on November 29, 2011.On December 14, 2011, RMD mailed IR letters to 5 purchasers identified by Pro Air.Three companies responded by filing Part 573 Reports and conducting safety recalls. Two companies, TMC Group and Herr Display Vans, did not respond to RMD?s IR letter or follow-up e-mails requests.These companies will be referred to NHTSA?s Office of the Chief Counsel for further possible enforcement action.In total, 9 manufacturers filed the following Part 573 Reports as a result of this EQ:11V-502 - Collins Bus Corp. 11V-540 ? Molly Corporation 11V-559 ? Double K, Inc. 11V-571 ? Starcraft Bus 11V-581 ? Kingmor Supply, Inc. 12V-003 ? Elkhart Coach 12V-011 ? Forest River, Glaval Bus Div. 12V-044 ? Turtle Top 12V-179 ? Nesco BusThis Equipment Query is closed.

subject: Williams Controls Accelerator Pedals
summary: On April 26, 2011, Pierce Manufacturing, Inc. (Pierce) notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain Pierce fire trucks, manufactured between June 22, 1999, and May 12, 2008, contain a safety related defect. Pierce stated that certain model year 1999 through 2008 Arrow XT, Dash, Lance, and Enforcer vehicles contain a Williams Controls, Inc. (Williams Controls) suspended electronic accelerator pedal that may become bent after repeated use with excessive force. If the pedal arm bends far enough, the pedal may contact the cab floor without warning and stick in the full throttle position. If the accelerator pedal becomes stuck, the operator may lose control of the vehicle increasing the risk of a crash. This issue was assigned recall number 11V-255.On May 12, 2011, RMD mailed an information request (IR) letter to Williams Controls requesting a list of customers who purchased the same or similar defective accelerator pedals.Williams Controls responded to RMD's IR letter on June 9, 2011 with a list those companies who purchased the same accelerator pedal.The list was submitted to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel under a request for confidentiality.Williams Controls' response letter outlined several key points.First, it was noted that these pedals, item number 131507, are generic parts that are purchased by engineering staffs in accordance with their own specifications.According to Williams Controls, Pierce modified their purchased pedals post-purchase and this modification reduced the strength of the accelerator pedal assembly.Also, Williams Controls stated that it has, never had a warranty claim or other notice, other than by Pierce on their modified pedal, due to lever arm permanent deformation for item number 131507.While Williams Controls submitted a list of companies that purchased item number 131507, it noted that it did not sell the same or similar defective pedal assemblies to any company as the subject pedals were modified by Pierce.This Equipment Query is satisfied as, because of modifications not conducted by the pedal manufacturer, the same or similar pedals were not sold to other vehicle manufacturers and no other vehicles should be affected.However, RMD will continue to monitor recall activity to see if any similar issues are found in other manufacturers' vehicles.This EQ is closed.

Pierce stated that certain model year 1999 through 2008 Arrow XT, Dash, Lance, and Enforcer vehicles contain a Williams Controls, Inc. (Williams Controls) suspended electronic accelerator pedal that may become bent after repeated use with excessive force. If the pedal arm bends far enough, the pedal may contact the cab floor without warning and stick in the full throttle position. If the accelerator pedal becomes stuck, the operator may lose control of the vehicle increasing the risk of a crash. This issue was assigned recall number 11V-255.On May 12, 2011, RMD mailed an information request (IR) letter to Williams Controls requesting a list of customers who purchased the same or similar defective accelerator pedals.Williams Controls responded to RMD's IR letter on June 9, 2011 with a list those companies who purchased the same accelerator pedal.The list was submitted to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel under a request for confidentiality.Williams Controls' response letter outlined several key points.First, it was noted that these pedals, item number 131507, are generic parts that are purchased by engineering staffs in accordance with their own specifications.According to Williams Controls, Pierce modified their purchased pedals post-purchase and this modification reduced the strength of the accelerator pedal assembly.Also, Williams Controls stated that it has, never had a warranty claim or other notice, other than by Pierce on their modified pedal, due to lever arm permanent deformation for item number 131507.While Williams Controls submitted a list of companies that purchased item number 131507, it noted that it did not sell the same or similar defective pedal assemblies to any company as the subject pedals were modified by Pierce.This Equipment Query is satisfied as, because of modifications not conducted by the pedal manufacturer, the same or similar pedals were not sold to other vehicle manufacturers and no other vehicles should be affected.However, RMD will continue to monitor recall activity to see if any similar issues are found in other manufacturers' vehicles.This EQ is closed.
