subject: Gunite Slack Adjusters Breaking
summary: On February 23, 2011, Accuride Corporation notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain Gunite branded automatic slack adjusters contain a safety related defect.Accuride stated that certain slack adjusters, manufactured between October 15, 2010, and January 31, 2011, contain inadequate structural integrity at the slack adjuster housing due to inadequate knitting of the iron at the time of casting.This inadequate structural integrity could cause the housing to break at the handle under normal operating loads.If the slack adjuster were to break, the wheel brake to which the slack adjuster is attached would no longer function, causing the vehicle to have reduced braking capacity and, if mounted on the steer axle, the vehicle could pull to one side, possibly resulting in a crash.This issue was assigned recall number 11E-008.Accuride's Defect Report also contained a purchaser list of vehicle manufacturers who were sold these slack adjusters.On August 4, 2011, NHTSA's Recall Management Division opened an equipment query (EQ) for this issue in order to write to these affected vehicle manufacturers.On September 8, 2011, RMD mailed information request (IR) letters to 15 manufacturers notifying them of the Accuride safety recall and requesting they conduct a safety recall for any new motor vehicles they manufactured with these slack adjusters.On November 3, 2011, RMD mailed a 2nd IR letter on November 3, 2011 to 5 manufacturers who did not respond to the first letter.Autocar Industries, Inc., Beall Transport of Montanna, and Kalmar Industries Corp., responded that their units were only sold into the aftermarket.These units would be covered under Accuride's safety recall.Manac Inc. and Polar Tank Trailer, LLC., responded that their only affected units were shipped to Canada and, thus, no U.S. safety recall is necessary.MAC Trailer Mfg., Inc. responded that the units they received did not fall within the production dates that Accuride recalled.Road Systems Incorporated responded that their affected inventory was returned to Accuride and no motor vehicles were affected.Three companies did not file sufficient responses to RMD's IR letters.Despite additional correspondence through phone calls and e-mails, Alfab, Inc. and Peerless Limited did not file a written response with RMD.E.D. Etnyre & Co. mailed RMD a large packet of notification letter copies and recall remedy receipts that they collected in the course of Accuride's recall.When RMD explained the regulatory requirement that E.D. Etnyre & Co. must notify the NHTSA of its defective vehicles via a Part 573 Defect & Noncompliance Information Report, the company chose not to respond.These three companies will be referred to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel for further enforcement action.In total, five manufacturers responded to RMD's IR letters by submitting Defect Reports and conducting safety recalls for their affected vehicles.Those companies are listed below:11V-479 - Silver Eagle 11V-481 - Wilson Trailer Company 11V-488 - Transcraft Corporation 11V-555 - Mertz Manufacturing LLC 11V-601 - Rosa Trailer Mfg.As RMD received adequate responses from all but three companies (as noted above), this Equipment Query is closed.

subject: TSE Brakes, Inc. Hill Hold Requirements
summary: On March 22, 2012, Spartan Motors Chassis, Inc. (Spartan) notified the NHTSA that it had decided a defect exists in certain model year 2012 K2 and MG chassis manufactured from December 15, 2011, through January 31, 2012, and equipped with 3030 brake chambers.These vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) Number 121, Air Brake Systems because they do not meet the park brake and draw bar requirements.The park brake may not hold the vehicle in place and if the vehicle moves, injury or property damage could occur without warning.NHTSA assigned recall number 12V-125 to this matter.Spartan reported that the manufacturer of the noncompliant brake chambers was TSE Brakes, Inc. (TSE).On April 9, 2012, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed an information request (IR) letter to TSE requesting a list of purchasers who received the noncompliant brake chambers, and also inquiring if TSE sold any affected brake chambers in the replacement market.In a letter dated April 20, 2012, TSE responded to RMD?s IR letter by explaining their non-concurrence with Spartan?s noncompliance decision. TSE noted that, to date, Spartan has provided three draw bar test results.The first test, dated November 29, 2011, ?significantly failed? while two tests dated February 7, 2012, ?significantly passed.?TSE concluded that these results ?ruled out the TSE actuator as an explanation? due to the actuators displaying the same output force yet having different test results.Also, TSE made note that there is no FMVSS requirement for actuator performance as FMVSS 121 compliance only relates to vehicle braking performance.The actuators used on Spartan?s 13 recalled chassis, according to TSE, meet industry standards per SAE J2318.TSE noted that these brake chambers are ?produced in Mexico and shipped to the U.S. for Spartan Motors only.?Irrespective of the differing views between TSE and Spartan, all chassis that could have been impacted by the reported noncompliance have been recalled.This EQ is closed.

TSE noted that, to date, Spartan has provided three draw bar test results.The first test, dated November 29, 2011, ?significantly failed? while two tests dated February 7, 2012, ?significantly passed.?TSE concluded that these results ?ruled out the TSE actuator as an explanation? due to the actuators displaying the same output force yet having different test results.Also, TSE made note that there is no FMVSS requirement for actuator performance as FMVSS 121 compliance only relates to vehicle braking performance.The actuators used on Spartan?s 13 recalled chassis, according to TSE, meet industry standards per SAE J2318.TSE noted that these brake chambers are ?produced in Mexico and shipped to the U.S. for Spartan Motors only.?Irrespective of the differing views between TSE and Spartan, all chassis that could have been impacted by the reported noncompliance have been recalled.This EQ is closed.

subject: Braun Wheelchair Lifts
summary: On January, 31, 2012, Braun Corporation (Braun) notified the NHTSA that it had decided a defect exists in certain Century-2 and Vista-2 wheelchair lifts, manufactured from November 20, 2006 through September 10, 2010, and installed on various vans and transit buses.Over time and with frequent use, the roll stop latches on the outer barrier may become bent or misaligned.Should this occur, a wheelchair occupant may defeat or ride over the insufficiently latched roll stop.If this occurs when the lift platform is in an elevated position, the wheelchair's occupant could fall and sustain injury.NHTSA assigned recall number 12E-002 to this matter.On April 30, 2012, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed an Information Request (IR) letter to Braun requesting a list of all customers that purchased the defective wheelchair lifts.On May 10, 2012, Braun submitted a list of purchasers to NHTSA?s Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) requesting confidentiality for its business records.On October 2, 2012, NCC responded to Braun?s request for confidentiality with a letter granting Braun?s request.On June 11, 2012, RMD mailed IR letters to sixteen (16) manufacturers that were detailed in Braun?s purchaser list.Seven (7) manufacturers chose to conduct safety recalls for their affected vehicles.Additionally, Forest River, Inc. submitted two (2) Part 573 Reports recalling both affected Forest River and Glaval Bus vehicles. Three (3) IR letters were undeliverable.Two (2) companies, Ameritrans Bus Company and Accubuilt, Inc. did not respond to RMD?s IR letter.Braun?s purchaser list also included a number of authorized dealerships that install and service Braun wheelchair lifts.RMD chose to contact twenty-seven (27) of these dealerships as they received sizable quantities of recalled wheelchair lifts which may have been installed on new vehicles.On August 21, 2012, RMD mailed an additional twenty-seven (27) IR letters these Braun dealerships.Twelve (12) companies provided responses explaining their product was returned, no actual defective product was received, or their units were not installed into new motor vehicles.Eight (8) companies filed Part 573 Reports and conducted safety recalls for their altered vehicles.Seven (7) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter.These nonresponsive companies were: Ride-Away Corporation, The Mobility Specialist, Cummings Mobility Conversions, Fenton Mobility Products, Advanced Wheels of Technology, Inc., and Gresham Driving Aids.In total, fifteen (15) companies filed Part 573 Reports with NHTSA and conducted safety recalls for this matter.The nine (9) companies that did not respond have been forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action.This EQ influenced the following safety recalls:12V-326 - Prime-Time Specialty Vehicle, Inc. 12V-292 ? Three (3) IR letters were undeliverable.Two (2) companies, Ameritrans Bus Company and Accubuilt, Inc. did not respond to RMD?s IR letter.Braun?s purchaser list also included a number of authorized dealerships that install and service Braun wheelchair lifts.RMD chose to contact twenty-seven (27) of these dealerships as they received sizable quantities of recalled wheelchair lifts which may have been installed on new vehicles.On August 21, 2012, RMD mailed an additional twenty-seven (27) IR letters these Braun dealerships.Twelve (12) companies provided responses explaining their product was returned, no actual defective product was received, or their units were not installed into new motor vehicles.Eight (8) companies filed Part 573 Reports and conducted safety recalls for their altered vehicles.Seven (7) of these companies did not respond to RMD?s IR letter.These nonresponsive companies were: Ride-Away Corporation, The Mobility Specialist, Cummings Mobility Conversions, Fenton Mobility Products, Advanced Wheels of Technology, Inc., and Gresham Driving Aids.In total, fifteen (15) companies filed Part 573 Reports with NHTSA and conducted safety recalls for this matter.The nine (9) companies that did not respond have been forwarded to NCC for possible enforcement action.This EQ influenced the following safety recalls:12V-326 - Prime-Time Specialty Vehicle, Inc. 12V-292 ? Molly Corporation 12V-344 ? Double K, Inc. 12V-404 ? Turtle Top 12V-281 ? Coach & Equipment Mfg. Corp. 12V-356 ? Eldorado National Kansas, Inc. 12V-293 ? Forest River, Inc. 12V-321 ? Forest River, Inc. / Glaval Bus 12V-427 ? Mobility Works 12V-442 ? Mobility Transportation Services, Inc. 12V-437 ? National Van Builders, Inc. 12V-433 ? Quality Van Sales, Inc. 12V-440 ? New England Wheels Inc. 12V-449 ? Mobility Services 12V-584 ? Creative Bus Sales, Inc. 12V-443 ? C&C MobilityThis EQ is closed.

summary: On January, 31, 2012, Braun Corporation (Braun) notified the NHTSA that it had decided a defect exists in certain Century-2 and Vista-2 wheelchair lifts, manufactured from November 20, 2006 through September 10, 2010, and installed on various vans and transit buses.Over time and with frequent use, the roll stop latches on the outer barrier may become bent or misaligned.Should this occur, a wheelchair occupant may defeat or ride over the insufficiently latched roll stop.If this occurs when the lift platform is in an elevated position, the wheelchair's occupant could fall and sustain injury.NHTSA assigned recall number 12E-002 to this matter.On April 30, 2012, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed an Information Request (IR) letter to Braun requesting a list of all customers that purchased the defective wheelchair lifts.On May 10, 2012, Braun submitted a list of purchasers to NHTSA?s Office of the Chief Counsel (NCC) requesting confidentiality for its business records.On October 2, 2012, NCC responded to Braun?s request for confidentiality with a letter granting Braun?s request.On June 11, 2012, RMD mailed IR letters to sixteen (16) manufacturers that were detailed in Braun?s purchaser list.Seven (7) manufacturers chose to conduct safety recalls for their affected vehicles.Additionally, Forest River, Inc. submitted two (2) Part 573 Reports recalling both affected Forest River and Glaval Bus vehicles. subject: Power Products Axle Missing Locking Ring
summary: On April 27, 2012, Reinke Manufacturing Company, Inc. (Reinke) notified the NHTSA that it had decided a defect exists in certain 2010-2013 intermodal chassis frames.On certain chassis frames, the locking ring that secures the spindle nut is missing from the axle or is improperly installed and the spindle nuts may be not be properly torqued.These conditions could lead to wheel separation which could cause the driver to lose control of the vehicle.Also, detached dual wheels may enter the roadway increasing the risk of a crash.NHTSA assigned recall number 12V-175 to this matter. Reinke identified Power Products World Wide Heavy Duty (Power Products) as the manufacturer of these defective axles.On June 7, 2012, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed an Information Request (IR) letter to Power Products requesting a list of purchasers that might have also received these defective axles.On June 18, 2012, Power Products responded with a written letter noting that Reinke was the only purchaser of these defective axles.All vehicles that could have been impacted by these defective Power Products axles have been addressed through Reinke's 12V-175 safety recall.This EQ is closed.

subject: Carlisle Wheel Separation
summary: On March 21, 2012, Carlisle Transportation Products (Carlisle) notified the NHTSA that it had decided a defect exists in certain 908 Yuma, 910 Intruder, and 921 Intrepid series Black Rock toy hauler trailer wheels.These trailer wheels were manufactured from August 9, 2010, through February 7, 2012, and were sold and installed as original equipment for use on various boat, camper, and utility trailer vehicles.These wheels were manufactured with machine dimensions for the application of a center cap and the application of steel lug inserts that were not controlled to the required blue print specifications.As a result, the wheel may not be tightened to proper torque requirements during the mounting process.This condition could allow the wheels to loosen, leading to wheel separation, and possibly a vehicle crash.A detached wheel also becomes a road hazard.This matter was assigned recall number 12E-011.On July 26, 2012, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed Information Request (IR) letters to ten (10) companies identified through a purchaser list submitted by Carlisle.On October 1, 2012, RMD mailed a second IR letter to three (3) companies that did not respond to the earlier letter.All companies contacted did eventually file a written response with RMD.Three (3) companies explained that their affected trailer wheels were returned to Carlisle prior to installation onto new or used trailers.The remaining seven (7) companies filed Part 573 Reports and conducted safety recalls for their affected trailers. The following seven (7) recalls were filed as a result of this EQ:12V-385California Trailer Works 12V-396B&M Mfg., Inc. 12V-414McClain Trailers 12V-418Lippert Components (Extreme Trailers) 12V-512Express Trailers 12V-517Forest River Texas Group 12V-520Aluminia, Inc.All wheels affected by this safety defect have been identified and a recall campaign conducted where applicable.Accordingly, this EQ is closed.

subject: SMI Bus Roof Escape Hatches / FMVSS 217
summary: In a letter dated April 18, 2012, Specialty Manufacturing, Inc. (SMI) notified the NHTSA that certain ProLo bus roof escape hatches, installed as original equipment on various school buses and transit buses, may fail to conform to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS).These hatches, shipped between April 1, 2011, and March 25, 2012, experience increased friction between the rear plate assemblies and the nylon rear pop-up support, resulting in an opening force that exceeds FMVSS No. 217, Bus Emergency Exits and Window Retention and Release.In the event of an emergency, a noncompliant hatch may not provide a means of readily accessible egress, increasing the risk of injury to the vehicle occupants.NHTSA assigned recall number 12E-017 to this matter.On July 12, 2012, RMD mailed information request (IR) letters to five (5) manufacturers who had not yet conducted safety recalls for this issue.Collins Bus responded that they did not incorporate these escape hatches into any new buses but instead sold them to dealerships.Collins noted that they would notify the dealers of SMI's recall.The other four (4) manufacturers filed Part 573 Reports and conducted safety recalls for their affected vehicles.The following recalls were filed as a result of this EQ:Turtle Top:12V-330 Elkhart Coach:12V-348 Girardin Minibus, Inc:12V-362 Glaval Bus:12V-384As RMD received adequate responses from all the companies it contacted, this Equipment Query is closed.

summary: On July 9, 2012, Deere & Company notified the NHTSA that it had decided certain John Deere 8.1 liter compressed natural gas engines, manufactured from June 2002 through January 2008, contain a safety related defect.Failures can occur within the engine turbocharger.The turbine or compressor wheel may fail, resulting in subsequent damage to the engine and/or an oil leak.Failure of the turbine or compressor wheel may result in smoke, fire and stalling.This issue was assigned recall number 12E-026.At the opening of this EQ, Deere & Company had not yet supplied several pertinent pieces of information as to its 12E-026 safety recall.On August 15, 2012, the Recall Management Division (RMD) mailed an information request (IR) letter to Deere & Company requesting: The number of engines containing this defect; its recall remedy plan; its recall reimbursement plan; the estimated date on which owner notification letters would be mailed; and a list of customers that purchased the affected engines.On August 24, 2012, Deere & Company submitted its written response where it detailed that 600 engines were affected by the recall.Deere & Company also noted that its remedy plan and reimbursement plan would be forthcoming, but were not yet available.Deere and Company mailed interim owner notification letters to its affected customers on September 5, 2012, but as of the closing of this EQ, no final remedy plan has been submitted.Per a telephone conversation with Deere & Company's counsel on November 20, 2012, it is now estimated that the remedy should be available the first week of March 2013.RMD will continue to monitor this recall's remedy and notification schedule.A purchaser list was also submitted by Deere & Company with their August 24, 2012 letter.The majority of defective engines were sold to Daimler Bus North America, New Flyer, and Thor Industries.Vehicles affected by these engines were recalled under 12V-447 (Daimler Bus), 12V-466 (New Flyer), and 12V-469 (Thor) shortly after receiving notification from Deere & Company.An additional one hundred and thirty-eight (138) engines were sold to two distributors, Bell Power Systems and Western Power Products.In order to learn if any other vehicle manufacturers received defective engines, on October 3, 2012, RMD mailed IR letters to both companies requesting a list of purchasers.After receiving no response from either company, a second IR letter was mailed to each company on November 15, 2012.Both Bell Power Systems and Western Power Products responded promptly with their respective purchaser lists.Their engines were not sold to any other vehicle manufacturers for use as original motor vehicle equipment.As all defective engines installed as original equipment will be recalled, this Equipment Query is closed.

subject: Brake S-Cam Tube Bracket Failure
summary: BACKGROUNDIn a letter dated January 15, 2012, Navistar, Inc. (Navistar) notified the NHTSA that it had decided a defect exists in certain Model Year 2012 and 2013 International brand ProStar and TranStar commercial trucks, manufactured from August 1, 2011 through June 12, 2012, and equipped with brake S-Cam tube bracket assemblies.The brake S-Cam tube bracket assembly on the steering axle may exhibit fractures between the wing bracket and the tube steel when mounted.According to Navistars filing, fractures between the wing bracket and the tube steel may result in an inoperative brake on the affected wheel end resulting in an unexpected pull condition during braking application or an unexpected increase in stopping distance.Either result may increase the risk of a vehicle crash.NHTSA assigned recall number 12V-546 to this matter.On May 28, 2013, the Recall Management Division (RMD) opened this Equipment Query Investigation in order to write to the company that supplied Navistar with these brake S-cam tube bracket assemblies, to notify the supplier of this defect, and to ensure thorough safety recalls are conducted where appropriate.An Information Request (IR) letter was sent to Meritor, Inc. (Meritor) on May 31, 2013 requesting: a list of original equipment vehicle manufacturers and after-market customers that purchased the affected brakes; the name, address and phone number of a contact for each customer; the quantity sold; the dates shipped; and, a defect report.MERITOR RESPONSEIn a letter dated June 13, 2013, Meritor responded to the IR letter and reported that based on its review of the data and information on the brake S-cam tube bracket assemblies, it did not believe these brake assemblies contain a safety related defect.Meritor investigated returned components and determined that fractures in the brake S-Cam tube bracket assemblies resulted from vehicle front-end system vibration; and, there were no defects in the design, material or manufacture of the returned components.Accordingly, Meritor stated that it will not file a defect report or conduct a recall of any equipment.However, as requested by RMD, Meritor provided a purchaser list identifying Navistar as the only purchaser of these brake S-Cam tube bracket assemblies. RECALL MANAGEMENT DIVISION ACTION All vehicle and replacement equipment manufacturers have been identified and have either filed a recall report and are conducting a recall, or have provided a response explaining why they do not believe the products they manufactured are defective.Accordingly, this equipment query is closed.

(Navistar) notified the NHTSA that it had decided a defect exists in certain Model Year 2012 and 2013 International brand ProStar and TranStar commercial trucks, manufactured from August 1, 2011 through June 12, 2012, and equipped with brake S-Cam tube bracket assemblies.The brake S-Cam tube bracket assembly on the steering axle may exhibit fractures between the wing bracket and the tube steel when mounted.According to Navistars filing, fractures between the wing bracket and the tube steel may result in an inoperative brake on the affected wheel end resulting in an unexpected pull condition during braking application or an unexpected increase in stopping distance.Either result may increase the risk of a vehicle crash.NHTSA assigned recall number 12V-546 to this matter.On May 28, 2013, the Recall Management Division (RMD) opened this Equipment Query Investigation in order to write to the company that supplied Navistar with these brake S-cam tube bracket assemblies, to notify the supplier of this defect, and to ensure thorough safety recalls are conducted where appropriate.An Information Request (IR) letter was sent to Meritor, Inc. (Meritor) on May 31, 2013 requesting: a list of original equipment vehicle manufacturers and after-market customers that purchased the affected brakes; the name, address and phone number of a contact for each customer; the quantity sold; the dates shipped; and, a defect report.MERITOR RESPONSEIn a letter dated June 13, 2013, Meritor responded to the IR letter and reported that based on its review of the data and information on the brake S-cam tube bracket assemblies, it did not believe these brake assemblies contain a safety related defect.Meritor investigated returned components and determined that fractures in the brake S-Cam tube bracket assemblies resulted from vehicle front-end system vibration; and, there were no defects in the design, material or manufacture of the returned components.Accordingly, Meritor stated that it will not file a defect report or conduct a recall of any equipment.However, as requested by RMD, Meritor provided a purchaser list identifying Navistar as the only purchaser of these brake S-Cam tube bracket assemblies. RECALL MANAGEMENT DIVISION ACTION All vehicle and replacement equipment manufacturers have been identified and have either filed a recall report and are conducting a recall, or have provided a response explaining why they do not believe the products they manufactured are defective.Accordingly, this equipment query is closed.
